measures.title: Charter amendment: Auditor enforcement of wage and workplace laws
measures.summary: Amends the Denver Charter to state expressly that the Auditor's Office may continue to enforce wage, worker protection, and other workplace rights laws as City Council provides by ordinance. The city's fiscal analysis says there is no anticipated fiscal impact because the Auditor already performs this work.
measures.yesMeans: The Charter is amended to list wage and workplace rights enforcement among the Auditor's duties.

measures.title: Charter amendment: budget and appropriation process
measures.summary: Amends the Denver Charter's budget and appropriation provisions to let City Council adopt, by ordinance, a two-year budget term, and modernizes or repeals certain Charter sections. It also moves the release of the Mayor's proposed budget from September 15 to the first Friday in September. The city estimates about $50,000 in one-time costs to reconfigure budget systems for a two-year budget.
measures.yesMeans: Council may adopt a two-year budget process, the proposed budget is released earlier, and the listed Charter sections are updated.
measures.noMeans: The Charter's current annual budget and appropriation process stays as it is.

measures.title: Charter amendment: Civil Service Commission and Department of Safety
measures.summary: Amends the Denver Charter to remove outdated language about the Civil Service Commission and Department of Safety, allow City Council to add Commission duties by ordinance, and allow probation periods to be extended for medical, military, or other approved leave. It also removes the Charter caps on the number of Fire Department (7) and Police Department (18) command assignments; the city's fiscal analysis estimates a minimal financial impact.
measures.yesMeans: The Civil Service and Department of Safety Charter provisions are updated as described, including removal of the command-assignment caps.

measures.title: Franchise agreement with Public Service Company of Colorado (Xcel Energy)
measures.summary: Approves a 20-year franchise agreement, starting January 1, 2027, with Public Service Company of Colorado (Xcel Energy) to use city streets and property to provide electric and gas service. It keeps the existing franchise fee of 3% of Xcel's applicable Denver revenues (about $34.3 million projected for 2027) and continues programs for undergrounding overhead power lines and emergency management coordination. The current franchise expires at the end of 2026.
measures.yesMeans: Denver approves the new 20-year franchise agreement with Xcel Energy.
measures.noMeans: The franchise agreement is not approved, and the current agreement expires at the end of 2026.

measures.title: Prohibition on force-feeding birds and sale of force-fed products, including foie gras
measures.summary: Adopts a city ordinance banning the force-feeding of birds in Denver and banning the sale of products made from force-fed birds, including foie gras, with an exception for veterinarians tube-feeding sick birds. Violations would carry civil penalties of $1,000 to $5,000 each, enforced by the Department of Public Health and Environment, with license suspension for repeated violations. It would take effect July 1, 2027.
measures.yesMeans: Force-feeding birds and selling force-fed bird products such as foie gras become prohibited in Denver.
measures.noMeans: No new city ban on force-feeding birds or on selling foie gras is adopted.

measures.title: Denver Public Schools (School District No. 1) mill levy override, up to $44 million annually
measures.summary: Raises Denver Public Schools property taxes by up to $44 million in 2026 (collected in 2027) and each year after, through a mill levy override, for educational purposes including educator pay, more career and technical education courses in high-demand fields, and student mental health and special education. Spending of the money would be reported in the district's annual independent audit, and investment earnings on it could be kept and spent as a voter-approved revenue change.
measures.yesMeans: Denver Public Schools may raise property taxes by up to $44 million a year for the listed educational purposes.
measures.noMeans: This Denver Public Schools property tax increase does not take effect.

measures.id: Front Range Passenger Rail District Ballot Issue 7A
measures.title: Front Range Passenger Rail District sales tax and debt for Colorado Connector (CoCo) rail service
measures.summary: Raises Front Range Passenger Rail District taxes by $295 million a year, through a 0.333% sales and use tax (one-third of a cent per dollar), and allows $580 million in district debt with a maximum repayment cost of $785 million. The money would build, operate, and maintain Colorado Connector (CoCo) passenger rail between Pueblo, Colorado Springs, Denver, Boulder, Fort Collins and other Front Range communities; state-law exemptions such as gasoline, food, residential utilities, prescription drugs and medical supplies apply. Revenues would be kept as a voter-approved revenue change and reviewed each year by an independent auditor and a rotating group of district taxpayers.
measures.yesMeans: The district may levy the 0.333% sales and use tax and take on the stated debt to build and run Front Range passenger rail.
measures.noMeans: The district's sales tax and debt are not approved.
